messages:
alex: Heads up — a few GPU training jobs in us-west-2a started failing 10m ago. They hang during checkpoint upload and RDMA-based shard syncs show timeouts. Seeing packet loss and a bump in intra-cluster latency. anyone else?

maria: :eyes: seeing increased retransmits on node nic stats. Which namespaces?

alex: namespace `inference-prod` mostly. Jobs schedule across AZs but traffic within the cluster (pod->pod) between AZa <> AZb is impacted. Autoscaler reported some backpressure too.

sachin: can you paste `kubectl get pods -n inference-prod -o wide` and `kubectl get networkpolicy -n inference-prod`? might be a netpol issue.

alex: quick outputs:

```
# kubectl get pods -n inference-prod -o wide
NAME                                 READY STATUS   RESTARTS AGE   IP            NODE
trainer-0                            1/1   Running  0        2h  10.42.3.12    ip-10-0-3-45.usw2a
trainer-1                            1/1   Running  0        1h  10.42.7.88    ip-10-0-7-22.usw2b
checkpoint-uploader-0                1/1   CrashLoop 5   12m 10.42.9.3     ip-10-0-9-11.usw2a
```

```
# kubectl get networkpolicy -n inference-prod
NAME                    POD-SELECTOR   AGE
deny-egress-waffle      app=waffle     3d
allow-only-ingress      app=ingress    1w
```

alex: Also ran `kubectl describe netpol deny-egress-waffle -n inference-prod` and it looks like a deny-by-default egress rule someone applied to lock down a third-party app.

maria: can you share the describe block? suspect it might be too broad and matching more pods than intended.

alex: pasted: 

```
Name:         deny-egress-waffle
Namespace:    inference-prod
PodSelector:  app=waffle
PolicyTypes:  Egress
Egress:
  to:
  - podSelector:
      matchLabels:
        role: sidecar
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 443
```

alex: The weird thing is we have RDMA traffic and intra-cluster non-TCP flows for NVLink/RDMA over Converged Ethernet. This netpol only allows TCP/443 to sidecars, so anything else gets dropped.

liza: ohh that `podSelector` might be catching our long-lived infra sidecar on GPU nodes. Who created this NP? `git blame` on infra overlay?

kyle: that policy was added by infra team to lock down waffle service egress to only talk to auth sidecar over HTTPS. But looks like label scoping was loose — some GPU sidecars have `role: sidecar` too (legacy labeling).

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-332 — "intra-cluster RDMA/egress drops affecting GPU jobs" (severity: high). Pagerduty alerted.

sachin: root cause hypothesis: overly-broad netpol with port restriction to TCP/443 + podSelector `role: sidecar` causing non-TCP RDMA (and some UDP/ICMP health checks) to be denied between pods across nodes. That would cause checkpointing and sync to fail and increase latency due to retransmits.

maria: confirms with packet capture on node ip-10-0-3-45:

```
# sudo tcpdump -i cni0 host 10.42.7.88 and not port 22 -c 20
listening on cni0, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet)
20 packets captured
ICMP echo request seq=1 ttl=63 time=151.3 ms
TCP 10.42.3.12.50000 > 10.42.7.88.50000: R ST, seq 0
RDMA_CM REJECT / timeout events (kernel logs)
```

maria: also saw MTU mismatch warnings earlier on some nodes (jumbo frames disabled in us-west-2b). RDMA over converged ethernet needs consistent MTU; combined with netpol drops it's a cascade.

alex: so fix path options: 1) roll back/patch the NP to restrict to the exact `app=waffle,env=prod` label set and remove port type restriction that blocks RDMA; 2) add an explicit Egress allow rule for non-TCP RDMA flows between pods with label `role: gpu-node`/`shard-sync: enabled`; 3) as temp mitigation, cordon/evict to force single-AZ scheduling (not ideal).

liza: I can prepare the NP patch. sample patch: 

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-waffle
  namespace: inference-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: waffle
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: waffle-auth
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:  # explicit allow for RDMA/cluster sync
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: gpu-node
    ports: []  # empty ports == allow all protocols
```

kyle: careful: some CNI implementations treat empty `ports` differently; better to add an explicit `to` without `ports` to allow all. Also need `namespaceSelector` if some gpu nodes live in different ns (they don't here).

sachin: +1 to patch. We should also add an audit rule that prevents future NPs from using generic `role: sidecar` label — create a doc and a helm chart lint check.

alex: rolling the patch now to staging, will watch traffic and job health.

ops-bot: Deploy started: patch/deny-egress-waffle v1 -> staging (by liza)

maria: after patch applied, ping between trainer pods within 15s: 2ms -> 3ms, no packet loss. RDMA sessions re-established for 3/3 shards. checkpoint uploader recovered.

alex: Verified training jobs resumed; autoscaler relieved. tagging this resolved for now but creating a follow-up to tighten label taxonomy and add NP pre-commit checks.

kyle: created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/issues/4521 "NetworkPolicy harden: forbid generic sidecar label + add NP lint"

liza: note for postmortem: include MTU mismatch check in GPU node onboarding checklist.

alex: nice job team :thumbsup: — moving to monitoring for 24h.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-2026-332 status -> resolved (24m elapsed).
